title: Using Cryptographic Libraries Safely
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of using cryptographic libraries safely in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply using cryptographic libraries safely in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to understanding implementation-specific requirements and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Using Cryptographic Libraries Safely through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding using cryptographic libraries safely helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Using Cryptographic Libraries Safely helps you reason about selecting maintained libraries. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Selecting maintained libraries. Then connect it to Correct use of standard algorithms. The remaining syllabus points—Key and nonce management concepts, Understanding implementation-specific requirements—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Using Cryptographic Libraries Safely
content_blocks.code:
def valid_username?(value)
  value.is_a?(String) && value.match?(/\A[a-z0-9_]{3,20}\z/i)
end
puts valid_username?("learner_7")
puts valid_username?("bad name")

items.text: Test an empty value, a boundary value, and one invalid value before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Treating an example as a universal rule

content_blocks.title: Guided example
